answer.answer: A standard operating margin doesn't work well for American Express. It is a card issuer and bank holding company, so its income statement has no operating income line: interest expense is a core cost of funding and is netted against revenue, and credit-loss provisions move sharply from year to year. Using pretax margin (pretax income ÷ total revenues net of interest expense) as the closest stand-in, the margin was not improving as of 2022: it fell to 18.1% in 2022 from 25.2% in 2021, after 11.9% in 2020, even though revenue grew 25% to $52.9 billion. Taking provisions out, margin before credit-loss provisions was roughly flat to slightly up (25.0% in 2020, 21.9% in 2021, 22.3% in 2022), so the 2022 drop mainly reflects the return to normal credit provisions rather than weaker core profitability.
answer.calculation:
Pretax margin = pretax income ÷ total revenues net of interest expense ($ millions):
- 2022: 9,585 ÷ 52,862 = 18.13%
- 2021: 10,689 ÷ 42,380 = 25.22%
- 2020: 4,296 ÷ 36,087 = 11.90%

Margin before credit-loss provisions = (pretax income + provisions) ÷ total revenues net of interest expense:
- 2022: (9,585 + 2,182) ÷ 52,862 = 22.26%
- 2021: (10,689 − 1,419) ÷ 42,380 = 21.87%
- 2020: (4,296 + 4,730) ÷ 36,087 = 25.01%

The 2021 provision was a net benefit of $1,419 million (reserve release), which inflated that year's pretax margin; 2022 had a $2,182 million charge.
